Tbh I was in a similar situation as you and also on a budget. I think you can just buy a decent graphics card and SSD such as a 1050ti. For SSD, it'll depend on how much money you have left but if your game library is bigger, get one close to 500GB. So, with a 1050ti, you don't need a huge PSU or anything and it can run games at your preference that you mentioned in your comment. I am currently running multiple games smoothly such as Apex Legends, Borderlands 2, CSGO, Portal, Hitman and more on my 1050 at 60fps and it's only running a 240W PSU. I can also run Battlefield 5 and Black Ops 4 which are the most graphics intensive games I own.

I might get downvoted by others but since you're on a budget, I think you should only think about buying those two components and not worrying about PSU upgrade until you actually build the PC.

On most instances, since you are on an HP prebuilt (me as well), it's gonna be super hard finding a new standard ATX PSU that can even fit (into the motherboard) without adapters since they are proprietary. I have a 8200 Elite SFF btw.
